title: Managing source IP groups with the ZTC Terraform provider and the Go SDK

prose.label: Lookups by name.
prose.text: The Go SDK's name lookup for source IP groups lists every group and matches case-insensitively: [[cloud-connector.sdk-go.lookups:same-pattern-elsewhere]]. {{case-collision}} {{import-by-id-or-name}}

prose.label: What the resource keeps in state.
prose.text: {{resource-read-fields}} Its `description` argument shares the provider multi-line handling: [[cloud-connector.terraform.provider-behavior:multiline-helpers-on-nine-resources]].

prose.label: Known defects.
prose.text: The SDK update for source IP groups shares the unchecked-assertion pattern: [[cloud-connector.sdk-go.service-defects:ztw-update-deref-same-pattern]]. Deletes detach the group from forwarding rules only: [[cloud-connector.terraform.delete-detach:ip-group-delete-follows-detach]].

checks.do: Whether two groups share a name that differs only in case before importing or looking a group up by name.
Use the data source, not the resource, when origin or editability is needed in Terraform.
Write `ztc_ip_source_groups` with `name` and `ip_addresses`, not the provider page's example type or argument list.

case-collision.statement: If two groups have names that differ only in case, a name lookup returns whichever the listing gives first, which may not be the intended one.
case-collision.conditions: Follows from the list-then-case-insensitive-match lookup, which also covers IP groups; whether the API allows such names was not checked.

import-by-id-or-name.statement: `ztc_ip_source_groups` imports by numeric ID, or, when the import ID is not numeric, by name through `GetByName`.

quotes: idInt, parseIDErr := strconv.ParseInt(id, 10, 64) if parseIDErr == nil { _ = d.Set("group_id", idInt) } else { resp, err := ipsourcegroups.GetByName(ctx, service, id)

resource-read-fields.statement: The `ztc_ip_source_groups` resource read copies only the ID, name, addresses and description into state; the data source also sets `creator_context` and `is_non_editable`.

quotes: d.SetId(fmt.Sprintf("%d", resp.ID)) _ = d.Set("group_id", resp.ID) _ = d.Set("name", resp.Name) _ = d.Set("ip_addresses", resp.IPAddresses) _ = d.Set("description", resp.Description) return nil

doc-example-wrong-type.statement: The provider's documentation page for `ztc_ip_source_groups` shows its create example as `resource "zia_ip_source_groups"`, the ZIA provider's resource type.

doc-arguments-wrong.statement: The same page's Argument Reference lists `name` as optional ('The name of the IP source group to be exported') and `id`, while the resource schema requires `name` and `ip_addresses`.

quotes: * `name` - (Optional) The name of the IP source group to be exported.
* `id` - (Optional) The ID of the IP source group resource.
"ip_addresses": { Type: schema.TypeSet, Elem: &schema.Schema{Type: schema.TypeString}, Required: true, },

zia-data-source-example.statement: The provider's `basic_forward_method_zia.tf` example looks up a source IP group with the ZIA provider's `zia_ip_source_groups` data source and passes its ID to `src_ip_groups` of a `ztc_traffic_forwarding_rule`.

zia-ids-accepted.statement: The example implies that the ID of a source IP group read through ZIA is a valid source IP group reference on a Cloud Connector forwarding rule.
zia-ids-accepted.conditions: Inferred from the provider example and from the help placing the page under Internet Access resources; no source states that ZIA and Cloud Connector share the group objects.
